audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for rotating military system, under-twenty exclusion, unfinished census and wrath, tribal representation, royal agricultural wealth, migrant/foreign managers, animal labor, counselor networks, Ahithophel context, nepotism, and public-private boundaries.

verses.restored: Children of Israel by number—ancestral heads, commanders of thousands and hundreds, and officers serving king in every matter of divisions—came in and went out month by month through all months; each division numbered twenty-four thousand.

familiar.text: Now the children of Israel after their number, to wit, the chief fathers and captains of thousands and hundreds, and their officers that served the king in any matter of the courses, which came in and went out month by month throughout all the months of the year, of every course were twenty and four thousand.

modern.text: This is the list of the Israelites—the heads of families, the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, and their officers who served the king in every matter concerning the divisions on rotating military duty each month throughout the year. There were 24,000 men in each division:

original.text: וּבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל לְֽמִסְפָּרָ֡ם רָאשֵׁ֣י הָאָב֣וֹת וְשָׂרֵ֣י הָֽאֲלָפִ֣ים וְהַמֵּא֡וֹת וְשֹׁטְרֵיהֶם֩ הַמְשָׁרְתִ֨ים אֶת הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ לְכֹ֣ל דְּבַ֣ר הַֽמַּחְלְק֗וֹת הַבָּאָ֤ה וְהַיֹּצֵאת֙ חֹ֣דֶשׁ בְּחֹ֔דֶשׁ לְכֹ֖ל חָדְשֵׁ֣י הַשָּׁנָ֑ה הַֽמַּחֲלֹ֨קֶת֙ הָֽאַחַ֔ת עֶשְׂרִ֥ים וְאַרְבָּעָ֖ה אָֽלֶף

verses.restored: Over first division for first month was Jashobeam son of Zabdiel; in his division were twenty-four thousand.

familiar.text: Over the first course for the first month was Jashobeam the son of Zabdiel: and in his course were twenty and four thousand.

modern.text: Jashobeam son of Zabdiel was in charge of the first division, which was assigned the first month. There were 24,000 men in his division.

original.text: עַ֞ל הַמַּחֲלֹ֤קֶת הָרִֽאשׁוֹנָה֙ לַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הָרִאשׁ֔וֹן יָֽשָׁבְעָ֖ם בֶּן זַבְדִּיאֵ֑ל וְעַל֙ מַֽחֲלֻקְתּ֔וֹ עֶשְׂרִ֥ים וְאַרְבָּעָ֖ה אָֽלֶף

verses.restored: He was from sons of Perez and chief of all army commanders for first month.

familiar.text: Of the children of Perez was the chief of all the captains of the host for the first month.

modern.text: He was a descendant of Perez and chief of all the army commanders for the first month.

original.text: מִן בְּנֵי פֶ֗רֶץ הָרֹ֛אשׁ לְכָל שָׂרֵ֥י הַצְּבָא֖וֹת לַחֹ֥דֶשׁ הָרִאשֽׁוֹן

verses.restored: Over division of second month was Dodai the Ahohite, and Mikloth was leader; in division were twenty-four thousand.

familiar.text: And over the course of the second month was Dodai an Ahohite, and of his course was Mikloth also the ruler: in his course likewise were twenty and four thousand.

modern.text: Dodai the Ahohite was in charge of the division for the second month, and Mikloth was the leader. There were 24,000 men in his division.

original.text: וְעַ֞ל מַחֲלֹ֣קֶת הַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַשֵּׁנִ֗י דּוֹדַ֤י הָאֲחוֹחִי֙ וּמַ֣חֲלֻקְתּ֔וֹ וּמִקְל֖וֹת הַנָּגִ֑יד וְעַל֙ מַחֲלֻקְתּ֔וֹ עֶשְׂרִ֥ים וְאַרְבָּעָ֖ה אָֽלֶף

modern.text: The twelfth, for the twelfth month, was Heldai the Netophathite, from the family of Othniel. There were 24,000 men in his division. The Leaders of the Twelve Tribes

familiar.text: But David took not the number of them from twenty years old and under: because the LORD had said he would increase Israel like to the stars of the heavens.

modern.text: David did not count the men aged twenty or under, because the LORD had said that He would make Israel as numerous as the stars of the sky.

original.text: וְלֹא נָשָׂ֤א דָוִיד֙ מִסְפָּרָ֔ם לְמִבֶּ֛ן עֶשְׂרִ֥ים שָׁנָ֖ה וּלְמָ֑טָּה כִּ֚י אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה לְהַרְבּ֥וֹת אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל כְּכוֹכְבֵ֥י הַשָּׁמָֽיִם

familiar.text: Joab the son of Zeruiah began to number, but he finished not, because there fell wrath for it against Israel; neither was the number put in the account of the chronicles of king David.

modern.text: Joab son of Zeruiah began to count the men but did not finish. For because of this census wrath came upon Israel, and the number was not entered in the Book of the Chronicles of King David. David’s Various Overseers

original.text: יוֹאָ֨ב בֶּן צְרוּיָ֜ה הֵחֵ֤ל לִמְנוֹת֙ וְלֹ֣א כִלָּ֔ה וַיְהִ֥י בָזֹ֛את קֶ֖צֶף עַל יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְלֹ֤א עָלָה֙ הַמִּסְפָּ֔ר בְּמִסְפַּ֥ר דִּבְרֵֽי הַיָּמִ֖ים לַמֶּ֥לֶךְ דָּוִֽיד

verses.restored: Over king's treasuries was Azmaveth son of Adiel; over storehouses in fields, cities, villages, and towers was Jonathan son of Uzziah.

familiar.text: And over the king’s treasures was Azmaveth the son of Adiel: and over the storehouses in the fields, in the cities, and in the villages, and in the castles, was Jehonathan the son of Uzziah:

modern.text: Azmaveth son of Adiel was in charge of the royal storehouses. Jonathan son of Uzziah was in charge of the storehouses in the country, in the cities, in the villages, and in the fortresses.

familiar.text: And over them that did the work of the field for tillage of the ground was Ezri the son of Chelub:

modern.text: Ezri son of Chelub was in charge of the workers in the fields who tilled the soil.

original.text: וְעַ֗ל עֹשֵׂי֙ מְלֶ֣אכֶת הַשָּׂדֶ֔ה לַעֲבֹדַ֖ת הָאֲדָמָ֑ה עֶזְרִ֖י בֶּן כְּלֽוּב

familiar.text: And over the vineyards was Shimei the Ramathite: over the increase of the vineyards for the wine cellars was Zabdi the Shiphmite:

modern.text: Shimei the Ramathite was in charge of the vineyards. Zabdi the Shiphmite was in charge of the produce of the vineyards for the wine vats.

modern.text: Baal-hanan the Gederite was in charge of the olive and sycamore trees in the foothills. Joash was in charge of the stores of olive oil.

original.text: וִֽיהוֹנָתָ֤ן דּוֹד דָּוִיד֙ יוֹעֵ֔ץ אִישׁ מֵבִ֥ין וְסוֹפֵ֖ר ה֑וּא וִֽיחִיאֵ֥ל בֶּן חַכְמוֹנִ֖י עִם בְּנֵ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ

translation_notes: Twelve rotating divisions create a permanent military system affecting soldiers, families, farms, and local economies even outside active war.
Excluding those twenty and under from the census is a meaningful limit, but the remaining system still raises conscription and consent concerns.
The unfinished census recalls chapter 21, showing that administrative counting and militarized control remain unresolved rather than inherently forbidden.
Tribal leaders do not guarantee full representation of women, poor people, local communities, or dissenters.
Royal property encompasses treasuries, storehouses, fields, vineyards, orchards, wine, oil, herds, camels, donkeys, and flocks, revealing a vast extraction and management system.
Farmers and animal keepers generate royal wealth; they require recognition, fair conditions, and protection from exploitation.
Obil the Ishmaelite and Jaziz the Hagarite hold trusted roles, undermining ethnic-purity narratives.
Animals are living beings cared for by workers, not merely royal inventory.
Ahithophel's later suicide in 2 Samuel 17 must remain visible; his name is not simply a neutral office-holder entry.
Family and companion appointments raise questions about nepotism and blurred public-private power.
safety_note: Do not glorify permanent militarization, conscription, royal extraction, nepotism, or ownership of workers and animals. Center underage protection, farmers, migrant managers, animal care, public accountability, and families carrying the hidden cost of rotating armies.
